sentences.text: This dinosaur grew to a maximum length of about 9 meters and weighed up to 4 metric tons.
A distinguishing feature is a prominent, short, solid crest-like structure located between the eyes.
Maiasaura peeblesorum is the only known species in the extinct genus Maiasaura.
The genus name Maiasaura means 'good mother lizard' in Greek.
The species was described by paleontologists Jack Horner and Bob Makela in 1979.
Remains were discovered in 1978, and the species was formally described the following year.
Whole eggs were found in 1979, marking the first complete dinosaur eggs discovered in North America.
Maiasaura has been designated as the official state fossil of Montana.
Maiasaura were herbivorous and terrestrial dinosaurs.
They could walk on two legs or four legs depending on their activity.
It is likely that the animal primarily escaped danger by fleeing in large herds.
Researchers suggest the eye crest may have been used for headbutting contests between males during breeding season.
Maiasaura peeblesorum is classified within the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
Maiasaura is classified as an ornithopod hadrosaurid dinosaur.
The genus Maiasaura was named by Horner and Makela in 1979.
The species Maiasaura peeblesorum was named by Horner and Makela in 1979.
Maiasaura lived during the late Upper Cretaceous period, approximately 76.7 to 70.6 million years ago, in the Campanian stage in what is now North America.
It lived alongside troodontids, the basal ornithopod Orodromeus, the dromaeosaurid Bambiraptor, and the tyrannosaur Daspletosaurus.

In the Oldman Formation of Alberta, it lived alongside various ceratopsians, dromaeosaurids, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus, thescelosaurids, pachycephalosaurs, ornithomimids, hadrosaurids, and the ankylosaurid Scolosaurus.
Studies by Saitta et al. suggest one sex of Maiasaura was roughly 45% larger than the other based on size statistics.
It is currently unknown whether the larger sex of Maiasaura was male or female.
It is debated whether the crest was used in head-butting contests between males during the breeding season.
It is debated whether the animal left the nest at the end of its first year or perhaps after another year.
